first.rationale: Onboarding simplification most directly addresses the simultaneous declines in completion and activation, with prior evidence of durable activation gains. Verify memory_86 to assess whether its adoption lift translated into qualified revenue, and memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but may create margin, retention, or customer-quality risks not resolved by the summarized acquisition and revenue lift.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable value. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower retention and failure through the first renewal cycle. Measure qualified revenue and longer-term retention before considering broad rollout.

final2.rationale: Proceed with the shortened-onboarding experiment. Verified evidence shows improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not react with promotional pricing: the verified 40% discount produced short-term revenue but 12% lower retention and failure through renewal. The competitor’s deeper cut raises near-term SMB churn risk, but it does not overturn that known downside; monitor churn and segment-level qualified revenue while testing onboarding.
